title: A bound on shared SST error limits the acceleration claim from five corrected products in 1985-2024
abstract: Five corrected SST products at 60S-60N give a mean quadratic coefficient of 0.02285 K per decade squared for January 1985 to June 2024. We derive sharp bounds on its bias from a shared error with bounded total variation. A budget of 0.1152 K can remove the mean coefficient and leave every product difference unchanged. A smooth shared error with a range of 0.0888 K does the same and leaves the linear trend unchanged. If the shared error is zero from 2005 onward and at the start, the required budget rises to 0.2225 K. A 24-month residual block bootstrap gives an interval of 0.00986 to 0.03498 for the coefficient. Its worst-case lower endpoint reaches zero at a shared-error budget of 0.0497 K. These are conditional sensitivity bounds, not evidence that such errors occurred. They specify a stability requirement for independent references. The calculation uses five available series from a prior seven-product correction, fixed controls and fixed corrections; it does not infer actual shared error or test radiative feedback.

display.caption: Sharp conditional bounds for shared-error total variation, a smooth witness, and unchanged product differences. The left range is not a confidence interval.

citations.reason: Uses five corrected regional series and the model library. Quantifies the stated common-error limitation and challenges treating product agreement as an absolute error bound.
